To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

rural teachers can self-assess for grading bias by asking questions such as: “What are the sources of my bias?” “How does my bias impact my grading?” “How might I reduce my bias?” “What resources are available for me to reduce my bias?” and “What are my next steps?”
teachers in rural schools are more likely to unintentionally grade students’ work in a biased manner than their counterparts in other schools, and they can take steps to reduce this tendency.

1) teachers’ unintentional bias in grading is a significant issue in rural schools; 2) there are multiple sources of unintentional grading bias; 3) teachers in rural areas are less likely to have the resources and opportunities to reduce grading bias; and 4) there are strategies to help teachers in rural schools reduce unintentional grading bias.
